questions.q: In late 2026 a startup with no existing Kendra usage wants a RAG chatbot over documents in S3 and Confluence. It wants a managed vector store and built-in answer generation with the least operations work. Which service should it use?

options.t: A new Amazon Kendra GenAI Enterprise index
options.why: Wrong: Kendra is in maintenance mode and closed to new customers since 30 July 2026.

options.t: Amazon OpenSearch Service with a k-NN index
options.why: Wrong: it works, but you design mappings, scaling and relevance yourself, and still call an LLM yourself.

options.t: Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
options.why: Right: AWS recommends it for new RAG work; it has S3 and Confluence connectors, a fully managed vector store and RetrieveAndGenerate.

options.t: A Kendra Basic Developer Edition index
options.why: Wrong: closed to new customers, and Developer Edition is for proof of concept only, not production.

questions.explain: New search/RAG builds go to Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base; Kendra is only for existing customers.
questions.remember: Kendra is in maintenance mode: existing customers keep full support, new customers cannot start. New RAG → Bedrock Managed KB; existing Kendra → keep it or migrate.
variants: The goal is a finished employee assistant with no custom UI → Amazon Q Business.
The team needs full control of analyzers, ranking and scale → OpenSearch.
The company already runs a Kendra GenAI index → use it as a retriever in Bedrock Knowledge Bases instead of rebuilding.

questions.q: A company already runs an Amazon Kendra index. A new application must send relevant text chunks from the index to an LLM, which writes the answer. Which Kendra API should the application call?

options.t: Retrieve
options.why: Right: it returns up to 100 semantic passages (chunks of up to about 200 tokens) ranked for RAG.

options.t: Query
options.why: Wrong: it returns ANSWER, DOCUMENT and FAQ result types for a search box, not passages ranked for an LLM.

options.t: BatchPutDocument
options.why: Wrong: it adds documents to the index; it does not search.

options.t: Rescore (Kendra Intelligent Ranking)
options.why: Wrong: it re-ranks results from another search engine such as OpenSearch; it does not read the Kendra index.

questions.explain: Passages for an LLM → Retrieve; answers, FAQs and documents for a search box → Query.
questions.remember: Retrieve = passages for RAG. Query = search results (extracted answer, documents, FAQ matches) with facets, sorting and suggestions. Both share the same QPS capacity.
variants: The search page needs facets, spell suggestions and FAQ answers → Query.
Results come from an existing OpenSearch cluster and need better semantic ranking → Kendra Intelligent Ranking (Rescore).
Documents come from a system with no connector → BatchPutDocument or export to S3.

questions.q: A Kendra Enterprise index syncs SharePoint with a connector that crawls the document ACLs. In testing, every employee can see restricted HR documents in the search results. What is the most likely cause and fix?

options.t: The index is not encrypted; add a customer-managed KMS key
options.why: Wrong: encryption at rest does not filter results by user.

options.t: The users lack kendra:Query in IAM; add it to their role
options.why: Wrong: without the permission they could not query at all; IAM does not filter documents.

options.t: Kendra cannot read SharePoint permissions; move the files to S3
options.why: Wrong: connectors crawl ACLs from sources such as SharePoint.

options.t: The app does not send user context; authenticate the user and pass their identity with each query
options.why: Right: if no user information is sent, Kendra returns all documents. User context filtering is not authentication, so the app must supply a verified identity.

questions.explain: No user context on the query → Kendra returns all documents, even when ACLs exist.
questions.remember: Document-level security needs both: ACLs on the documents (crawled, metadata file or Principal list) and an authenticated user identity sent with every Query/Retrieve. Documents with no ACL are public.
variants: Nobody sees restricted documents → user/group strings do not match the ACL (email vs account ID, case).
Access must be revoked without re-indexing (S3 or BatchPutDocument docs) → CreateAccessControlConfiguration.
The index is GenAI Enterprise → only user attributes in AttributeFilter work; token-based control is not supported.

questions.q: A Kendra Enterprise index serves a search page (Query) and a RAG bot (Retrieve). Since the bot launched, both get throttled at peak hours. The document count is well below the storage limit. What should the team do?

options.t: Add storage units
options.why: Wrong: storage units add documents and extracted text, not queries per second.

options.t: Add query units
options.why: Right: QPS is shared by Query and Retrieve, and each Enterprise query unit adds 0.1 QPS.

options.t: Create a second Developer Edition index for the bot
options.why: Wrong: Developer Edition is not for production and cannot add capacity units.

options.t: Run the data source sync less often
options.why: Wrong: sync frequency changes connector cost, not query throughput.

questions.explain: Throttling on Query/Retrieve → QPS exceeds capacity → add query units.
questions.remember: Kendra capacity is bought in units: query units for QPS (shared by Query and Retrieve), storage units for documents/GB. Billing is hourly per provisioned capacity, even when idle.
variants: The index is full (documents or GB over the limit) → add storage units or prune.
Costs are high but usage is low → delete or downsize units, or move to Bedrock Managed KB.
A cheap test index is needed → Developer Edition or the GenAI free trial, then delete it.

questions.q: A company is migrating from Kendra to Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base. One Kendra data source is ServiceNow, which has no managed BMKB connector. Answers can be a few hours old. What is the simplest way to keep this content in the knowledge base?

options.t: Keep calling BatchPutDocument, now against the knowledge base
options.why: Wrong: BatchPutDocument has no direct BMKB equivalent; content must be uploaded to S3 and then ingested.

options.t: Point the knowledge base at the existing Kendra ServiceNow connector
options.why: Wrong: Kendra connectors sync into a Kendra index, not into a Bedrock Managed KB.

options.t: Export ServiceNow content to S3 on a schedule with metadata sidecar files, then start an ingestion job
options.why: Right: S3 is supported by BMKB; an EventBridge/Lambda schedule controls freshness and .metadata.json files carry attributes for filters.

options.t: Load the content into an OpenSearch index and query both systems
options.why: Wrong: adds a second search engine to run and tune for one data source.

questions.explain: No BMKB connector → scheduled export to S3 with metadata files, then StartIngestionJob.
questions.remember: BMKB has 7 connectors (S3, Confluence, SharePoint, Web Crawler, Google Drive, OneDrive, custom) vs Kendra's ~32+. Anything unsupported → export to S3 with metadata sidecars and ingest.
variants: The app relied on Kendra autocomplete → OpenSearch suggester or an LLM completion service.
The app relied on Kendra synonyms (thesaurus) → expand the query in the app.
The app relied on Custom Document Enrichment → pre-process with Step Functions/Lambda before writing to S3.
